dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "R: 90 annual rows (DLR-104/219) by dealer x posted-month vs L: rows_accepted, cash_total_usd."
"R: 0 dup recharge_id or source_event_id, 0 dup on (subscriber_id, eff date, amount, plan_id), distinct subscriber_id 90, self-join in [eff, +365d) returns 0."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The March shift is benign process, not concealment: visible, consistent, reconciling."
"Compare posted_at with effective_event_date" is operationalized through the finding that "May effective dates run 1-28 May" while dealer-specific annuals have delayed posting lags.

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Medium on reporting: a posted_at-keyed trend pack carries an artificial month-end step, a presentation defect."
"Recognition basis - highest impact... No GL in the pack, so I cannot tell whether the $1,506.29 of May annual cash was recognised in May or deferred."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Run a read-only recognition trace: pull the May GL export and trace the 17 source_event_ids of the 31 May batch to their revenue lines."
"A read, not a posting - no journal, no reversal, no re-post."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Decision rule, fixed before the result:"
"Deferred across the term... close it with a read-only re-cut of the trend pack on effective_event_date"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "one batch, not 17 events" is stronger than the cited recharge filter alone establishes; the rows being in the same hour does not by itself prove a single batch.
"No aggregate spike" is rhetorically overstated: 210 rows was still the sixth-busiest posting date, even if the annual subset was unusually concentrated.
"Pipeline defect: killed by rows 3, 4" overstates the conclusion because the log covers only 90 annual rows from two dealers and completeness outside that scope remains unknown.

"No backdating or stuffing" is stronger than the cited evidence supports; same-month effective dates and clean lags reject one form of cross-month leakage but do not by themselves rule out every form of reporting manipulation.
"Recognised point-in-time in May: May revenue is overstated by up to $1,506.29" is conditional and may not be an overstatement without first establishing the applicable revenue-recognition basis.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A legitimate posting-time quirk may coexist with a material accounting or control issue: the two dealers could be incomplete or contractually noncompliant, entitlements could fail to activate, or revenue could be recognized on an inappropriate basis. The submission largely handles these alternatives by identifying missing GL, dealer-master, contract, and provisioning evidence, but its headline high-confidence rejection is somewhat stronger than those unknowns warrant.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Qualify the headline conclusion and rejection language to match the limited scope: explicitly state that duplicate cash and entitlement integrity are cleared only for the 90 traced dealer rows, then obtain the dealer master, completeness evidence, and GL recognition trace before asserting that there is no material issue.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: [Fact] Pre-auth terminations tripled: terminal_stage=authenticate on 24.0% of NOVA sessions vs 7.9% South-LEGACY.
[Fact] The problem rate did not fall: South outages held at 10 events / 9,409 accounts in May and 8 / 7,045 in June, in line with Jan-Apr, yet NO_SIGNAL cases fell 51 to 28.

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: [Causal claim, med-high] NOVA-S1 caused part of the decline by adding an auth gate that kills contacts before they are logged, and by collapsing the transfer path that created cases.
[Inference, med-high] Part of the drop is real: balance_check 29.1% and pack_info 21.3% are NOVA-only stages.

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: [Unknown] No repeat-contact data exists in the three files; that is what would settle whether deflected customers were helped or dropped.
Rejected, each with what would have to be untrue to survive: 1. Self-service improved CX. Killed by the outage and pre-auth rows...

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: Do not expand NovaIVR nationally yet: the South decline is not clean evidence that CX improved; it is mostly a measurement-and-auth artifact.
Nothing is rolled out and nothing is switched off. The one step I would take is reversible: a read-only pull of 7-day repeat-contact rates...

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: The one step I would take is reversible: a read-only pull of 7-day repeat-contact rates, any channel, for the 411 South subscribers who hit an auth failure, against a matched E/N/W cohort.
What conditions make NOVA-S1 create a CareDesk case rather than resolve-and-close or transfer, and what changed from LEGACY, given case creation fell 49.5% to 3.3%?

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Those failures never become complaints” is too strong: the cited absence of a case establishes missing case creation, not that the underlying contacts were not complaints or that no later complaint occurred.

“Part of the drop is real: balance_check 29.1% and pack_info 21.3% are NOVA-only stages” is not established by stage presence alone; these stages could represent attempted or failed self-service rather than successful resolution.

“Self-service improved CX. Killed by the outage and pre-auth rows” overstates the inference. Stable outage exposure and increased pre-auth failures strongly undermine ticket-count evidence, but they do not by themselves rule out some CX improvement in successfully completed journeys.

“Dev Khanna owns billing, ruled out by the outage row” is insufficiently supported as a general ruling-out of billing-related explanations; the outage comparison mainly addresses service exposure and NO_SIGNAL cases.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handles the key benign alternative that lower tickets could reflect successful self-service rather than lost complaints by preserving repeat-contact and journey-fate unknowns and proposing a matched-cohort test. It misses a more nuanced version in which the pilot genuinely improves outcomes for successfully completed balance or package-information journeys while simultaneously losing some complaint cases at authentication; the evidence supports measurement failure but does not quantify the balance between these effects.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add end-to-end journey validation, including sampled listening or record review of pre-auth and supposedly resolved sessions, linked to later contacts, cases, and verified successful outcomes; do not use repeat-contact parity alone as the expansion gate.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: Observed and well-cited: the submission identifies inverter_events.csv lines 2-5, names the relevant fields, and lists all four inverter IDs, timestamps, severities, durations, impacts, and cleared values.
Inference appropriately labeled: completeness is described as untestable because the seven CSV fields contain no scope, filter, fleet-size, or total-count field.

Minor overreach: “no event in this file supports escalation” treats severity, cleared status, and zero impact as more dispositive than the export alone establishes, especially for FAN_SPEED_HIGH and DC_INPUT_CHECK.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission cross-checks impact_mw, cleared, severity, duration, recurrence by inverter_id, and date coverage rather than relying on a single field.
It genuinely rejects recurrence as a developing single-inverter fault using the directly measurable fact that all four inverter IDs are distinct.

The mechanism analysis is incomplete: it does not test whether the mixed event names have documented meanings or whether a cleared zero-impact FAN_SPEED_HIGH could still merit a low-priority equipment check.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The analyst explicitly qualifies the constant zero impact field: “consistent with zero impact rather than proof of it.”
They distinguish high confidence in the observed row-level facts from medium confidence about export completeness and identify the missing denominator.
They state the smallest decision-changing evidence—filter parameters and the plant-wide event count—rather than requesting broad additional investigation.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation—“ask whoever generated this export for its filter parameters and the plant-wide event count”—is cheap, reversible, and directly discriminates between a complete export and a slice.
The decision not to escalate four cleared, zero-impact, non-repeating rows is proportionate to the supplied evidence and avoids inventing a plant problem from a short communications warning.
The action could be slightly stronger by pairing the scope check with event-definition confirmation, but the proposed check is operationally sound.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion is accurately scoped to the four exported events: no incident is raised and no escalation is recommended for those rows.
It preserves the key qualification that completeness is unknown and specifies what would trigger a re-pull.
This matches the best-supported reading: zero MW impact, rapid clearing, and no inverter recurrence do not justify escalation, while export completeness remains the only material uncertainty.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “No event in this file supports escalation” is somewhat too categorical: cleared status, severity, and zero impact support non-escalation, but do not by themselves establish that FAN_SPEED_HIGH or DC_INPUT_CHECK has no equipment significance.

The rejected hypothesis says equipment failure would require impact_mw > 0, cleared = no, or severity error/critical. That requirement is unsupported; an equipment-related alarm could be cleared, have zero measured MW impact, and still warrant a low-priority quality or maintenance check.
The submission does not establish that the event names are merely benign communications or checks; it only establishes that the recorded rows show no impact and were cleared.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The export may be a filtered slice rather than the full plant event population, and the mixed event labels could include a transient communications warning plus non-impacting equipment-condition alarms. Even if the export is complete, those labels might justify a low-priority event-definition or alarm-history check without supporting operational escalation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: After confirming export scope and the plant-wide count, obtain the documented meanings or source alarm records for FAN_SPEED_HIGH and DC_INPUT_CHECK; this would test the only remaining plausible equipment-significance alternative without launching a broad investigation.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites specific fields and row counts, including `dispatch_blocks.csv`, 96 rows per day, `base_schedule_mw`, `submitted_schedule_mw`, `actual_mw`, `dsm_penalty_rs`, and `schedule_source`.
It distinguishes reconstructed observations from inference, explicitly labeling the fixed-actual causal interpretation as an assumption and identifying the band-rebuild residual.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It notices that the 31.6% comparison uses different days and constructs a same-day counterfactual by repricing 29 May using `base_schedule_mw` against fixed `actual_mw`.
It tests multiple alternatives: band crossing, forgone energy value, firmware differences, hindsight timing, and whether the revision was a flat offset or forecast-driven.
The analysis identifies the two mis-targeted NORMAL blocks and contrasts their penalty increase with savings from the ten STOW blocks.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission clearly distinguishes the observed pilot-day improvement from a causal estimate: 'An identified effect on one day - not a rate, no basis for a fleet or business case.'
It identifies decision-changing unknowns, especially submission timing, generality across additional stow days, forecast provenance, and firmware consistency.
The recommendation is conditional rather than certain: timestamps ahead of metering plus forecast-driven behavior would support continued piloting, while hindsight timing would stop it.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to hold the 31.6% claim internally, query submission times, and reconcile the workbook output is proportionate and reversible.
The proposed shadow-run preserves operational constraints while directly testing ex-ante timing and repeatability.
The pre-specified decision rule—expand only if deltas are negative on a clear majority of days and mis-targeted blocks are included—is a discriminating next test.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion keeps a smaller same-day benefit rather than incorrectly concluding there was no value: 'the pilot cut DSM penalty by Rs 96,476, or 17.55%, on 29 May.'
It correctly rejects publication of 31.6% as a controlled pilot effect while preserving the directional evidence from the same-day repricing.
It accurately scopes the result to one day and does not generalize it to a fleet or business case.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that 'no delivered MWh is given up' is an inference from zero observed `curtailment_mw` and fixed actual generation, not a fully demonstrated causal fact about what would have happened under the alternative schedule.
The phrase 'It returns on repetition' is overstated or unclear: blocks 63-64 demonstrate that two mis-targeted blocks increased penalty, but do not establish repeatability across future days.

The stated arithmetic should be reconciled: Rs 549,664 minus Rs 453,086 equals Rs 96,578 using the rounded figures shown, not Rs 96,476; this may reflect unrounded source values but should be explained.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 17.55% figure is a useful same-day fixed-actual repricing scenario, but it may still overstate the causal pilot effect if the base schedule is not a genuine untreated schedule, if the revision was made after generation information became available, or if changing the schedule could have affected actual generation. The submission appropriately identifies these as unresolved rather than treating the repricing as definitive proof.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain authoritative submission timestamps for the 12 revised blocks and compare them with the relevant metering and forecast cutoffs; this most directly determines whether the same-day saving was an ex-ante pilot effect or hindsight repricing.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "FACT: declared code is jurisdiction-correct - 90211000, effective 2025-01-01, Effective To blank, current on the 2025-11-04 entry" is tied to "country_tariff_matrix.xlsx, Swiss Matrix row 2 ...; declaration.pdf line 1".
"FACT: the benchmark is not a customs authority" is tied to "product_master_current.xlsx, Product Master row 2, Read Me rows 5, 7".
"INFERENCE: the flag is an artifact of that gap - schema seen, not the tool" appropriately states the limitation that only the schema, not the flagging tool, was inspected.
"duty 0.0% either way" and "the flag closes against the comparator, not the broker" are not given a clearly identified supporting source.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Rejected - Swiss Matrix row 2 would have to hold a different code, or an Effective To before 2025-11-04. Neither." tests the keying-error hypothesis against code and effective-date evidence.
"Rejected - its Read Me would have to grant ruling status; row 7 says the opposite, row 5 allows a mapping." directly tests the hypothesis that Helios is authoritative.
"A code there other than 90211000 changes my decision to escalate" identifies a concrete condition that would reverse the conclusion.
The submission separately identifies the invoice discrepancy and does not treat the code mismatch as the only possible issue: "Line != Qty x Unit" and "the packing basis ...".

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The evidence table distinguishes "FACT", "OBSERVED", and "INFERENCE" rather than presenting all claims as equally certain.
"INFERENCE: unit count undetermined (10/1/4) ... - but a labelling quirk or pieces-as-cartons fits equally" appropriately keeps multiple explanations open.
The submission explicitly rates the unresolved unit-count inference "Low" confidence and identifies missing evidence: "no packing basis" and "a packing list".
"if the declared code is Helios-sourced, not Tares, the match is coincidence and I re-open" is a suitably conditional treatment of source lineage.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Two systems are being compared" and "90211000 is the approved Swiss code ... 90211090 commercial master data" explain the jurisdiction/master-data distinction underlying the apparent mismatch.

"different nomenclatures, same harmonised code - EU uses CN8, Switzerland a local code, cross-jurisdiction matching not expected" identifies the code-system mechanism rather than inferring misconduct from the mismatch.

"hts_code is string(8) padded/truncated; code-system, version, effective dates not modeled" connects the schema limitation to a plausible false-positive mechanism, while acknowledging "schema seen, not the tool".
"normalise to HS6 before flagging" proposes a system-level remediation consistent with the identified cross-jurisdiction mismatch.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Do not escalate as a declaration error" is proportionate to the evidence that the Swiss code is current and the benchmark permits mappings.
"Hold the flag open; ask the Swiss country owner to confirm P1001 in Tares - one query, nothing to the broker, nothing amended" is a limited, reversible verification step.

"Qty confirmed at 10 and I put the line on valuation hold and pull the packing list, before any amendment is drafted" avoids unsupported amendment or compliance action while addressing the material invoice discrepancy.
The response provides explicit escalation triggers: "A Tares code other than 90211000 and I escalate".

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "90211000 is the approved Swiss code" is somewhat overstated because the submission itself says the Swiss Matrix requires confirmation in Tares for legal use; the matrix establishes a current candidate code, not necessarily legal approval.
"duty 0.0% either way" lacks a cited tariff or duty-rate source in the evidence table.
"the flag closes against the comparator, not the broker" is asserted without direct evidence from the flagging tool or workflow logs.

"the unchecked invoice is the real problem" is directionally reasonable, but the quantity/value discrepancy remains unresolved and could be a labeling or packaging convention rather than a confirmed valuation error.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent code error may be a benign Swiss-versus-EU nomenclature and master-data mismatch, but a genuine declaration issue remains possible if Tares assigns a different Swiss code or if the Helios value was used as the declaration source. Independently, the invoice's quantity, piece count, and declared value may reflect a real valuation or documentation problem, although the current evidence does not establish which unit basis is correct.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide direct evidence from the flagging workflow and tariff-rate records, while changing "approved Swiss code" to the more precise "current Swiss Matrix code pending Tares confirmation."

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "FACT: preference claimed, nothing linked - Preference = Yes on the only line, entry 2025-09-18" tied to "declaration.pdf line 1" and "review_note.txt sole line"
"FACT: the declaration the lookup ran expired 7 weeks before the entry" tied to "supplier_origin_register.csv line 10" and "supplier_declaration_reference.txt"
"FACT: absence from the register is not proof of non-origin" tied to "supplier_declaration_reference.txt line 2" and "origin-workshop.md, Procurement rep turn"
"OBSERVED, read separately (valuation, independent of preference)" tied to the invoice, AWB and declaration

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission explicitly lists and rejects competing hypotheses, including "The indicator being set means the claim is supported," "SUP-02's Irish declaration covers the entry," and "ERP says US, so the claim is false - reject it."
"Rejected as over-reaching - 'false' needs evidence that no qualifying document exists anywhere."
"The route, the Irish consignee, or the 0% rate settles it." is rejected because movement and tariff outcome do not establish preferential origin.
"Which supplier sourced this shipment" and "The agreement and origin criterion invoked" are identified as unresolved tests.

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The preference claim is not supported by anything in this packet... and it is not proven false, so this is hold-and-verify, not rejection or fraud."
The evidence table distinguishes "High," "Med" and "Low" confidence, including low confidence for the quantity inference.
"Not established is not disproved."
"Fraud referral only if a document is asserted then not produced - never on the register gap alone."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "ERP/Helios cannot decide this either way - it carries manufacturing country, 'never designed to prove preference'" tied to "origin-workshop.md, 3 Oct 2025, Ferri and Brennan."
"the register is 'not always updated', declarations sit in category folders" explains why register absence is not dispositive.
"No packet field records" the sourcing supplier, identifying a data-lineage gap rather than treating the current rows as conclusive.
"a valid one there means the register is the defect, not the declaration" identifies a plausible system-process explanation.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "this is hold-and-verify, not rejection or fraud" is proportionate to the evidence.
"Nothing is amended or filed, no revenue moves at 0.0%, and the hold reverses the moment a document appears."
The proposed request is specific: "the current P1006 declaration for this entry, the sourcing supplier, and the rule invoked."
The submission safely separates the valuation issue: "it does not affect the preference call" and recommends to "pull the packing list" before any amendment.

A minor limitation is the categorical instruction "not produced by the deadline and I correct the indicator to non-preferential" without stating that the deadline or correction procedure is authorized by the applicable control policy.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "SUP-01/P1006 = United States ... and it is non-qualifying" is stronger than the packet evidence unless the applicable agreement and origin rule establish that US origin cannot qualify; the submission itself correctly notes that the agreement and criterion are still missing.
"This one item decides the case" is slightly overstated because a declaration alone may not settle the claim without verifying the applicable agreement, rule and linkage to the shipment.
"Produced and valid, I clear preference" may be too categorical without confirming the document's substantive origin criterion and shipment linkage.
"Duty is 0.0% either way" is presented as fact but the cited evidence should be checked to confirm that the rate is independent of the preference treatment and not merely the declared outcome.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The shipment may have been sourced from SUP-03, SUP-05 or SUP-06, each showing a current EU-origin P1006 declaration, while the US declaration and expired Irish row belong to other supplier records or reflect stale/misaligned register data. Alternatively, the claim may rely on a preferential-origin rule not captured by manufacturing country; therefore the packet supports a documentation and data-lineage failure, not a false claim or fraud finding.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the decision rule conditional on verifying the applicable agreement and origin criterion: obtain the shipment-linked supplier evidence and rule, then assess substantive qualification rather than treating any current declaration as automatically sufficient.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "185 of 262 release stamps are exactly 02:10:00"; "source_freshness.csv QCore row, daily"
"(lab -> release) mod 24 h equals ... (02:10 minus lab_complete time-of-day) ... max deviation 0.016 h"
"median lab -> release falls 21.3 -> 8.4 h (n=35)"
"INFERENCE: a dashboard reporting ~5.5 h inverts the live queue" is explicitly labeled as inference and notes scope uncertainty.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "the sub-day part of the duration is arithmetically fixed by what time of day the lab finished, not by how long disposition took" separates the apparent symptom from a timestamp mechanism.
The proposed test—"pull the true disposition timestamp from live QCore for ten batches"—directly discriminates a snapshot default from genuine 02:10 dispositions.
The submission triangulates timestamp concentration, arithmetic structure, censoring by receipt date, and live HOLD ageing rather than jumping from one anomaly to a cause.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: Confidence is claim-specific in the evidence table, including "High on the waits; Med on 'inverts' - assumes these rows are in target scope."
"Nothing here tests that" appropriately limits the claim about missing certificates.
"The catalog definition ... If it states the field carries date only ... no spot-check is needed" and the event-log request make missing semantics decision-relevant.
The analysis does not fully articulate the possible non-coherent snapshot relationship between all source extracts, although it does request aligned extracts.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "I would not let this extract become a KPI tomorrow" is a clear decision change based on measurement validity, not merely process performance.
"Smallest verification, one check" proposes a focused, reversible validation before building a dashboard.
The recommendation protects against optimizing a measurement artifact and proposes an operationally useful alternative: measure the open HOLD cohort as ageing work-in-progress.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission tests and rejects competing explanations including "A day and a half is a real cycle time," "The data is broken - discard it," missing certificates, HOLD as a quality signal, and publishing the mean with a caveat.
It states what could revive the main alternative: "Ten that are real 02:10 dispositions and my central objection collapses."
The certificate hypothesis is not over-rejected: "A control breach needs the live portal to show no certificate; nothing here tests that."

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "pull the true disposition timestamp from live QCore for ten batches" is a small, high-value discriminating query.

The submission additionally requests "an agreed metric definition" and "event-level QCore logs, or extracts aligned to one snapshot time," tying each request to a decision about KPI validity and WIP ageing.
It prioritizes the live timestamp check ahead of the catalog lookup and explains why: "the spot-check answers either way."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "HOLD tracks receipt date perfectly ... it means 'arrived last week, not yet dispositioned in this snapshot'" is a strong semantic conclusion from temporal association; the pattern supports snapshot censoring but does not by itself prove the HOLD meaning.

"every cycle-time figure built on it is invalid" is broader than the evidence strictly establishes: the timestamp may still be an operational interface-commit measure, though it is unsuitable for the stated decision-time KPI unless defined accordingly.
The opening comparison of "45.5 h to 5.5 h" mixes different endpoint/exclusion definitions, so it is rhetorically useful but not a like-for-like estimate of one unchanged metric.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 timestamps could be genuine batch/interface processing or release-commit times rather than a default snapshot value. In that case they may support a valid interface-latency KPI, but not necessarily a decision-time QC cycle KPI; the field definition and event-level decision timestamps would discriminate this interpretation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain a small event-level QCore audit extract for the ten 02:10 batches, including decision/disposition time, interface commit time, extract snapshot time, and source lineage. This would distinguish workflow delay from interface timing more reliably than a live spot-check alone and establish whether the cross-source joins are temporally coherent.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "An exact join on manufacturer_part_no resolves all 13 requests carrying one" and the candidate table identifies request IDs, stock locations, quantities, revisions, and availability conditions.
The evidence table cites part_requests.csv, spare_parts.csv, part_restrictions.csv, and source_freshness.csv, including the $166,495.60 recalculation and specific reserved stock rows.

"The stock view is a month older than the requests" is directly tied to MaintStar-global 2026-06-26 versus ProcureNet 2026-07-24; however, the claim that all 13 exact joins are resolved is not independently shown row by row in the submission.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: The submission separates matching from transferability: "The search found a match, so transfer it." is rejected because MT-18 gates identity, revision, UOM, qualification, and reservation.

It triangulates request identity, stock, restrictions, and freshness, and distinguishes local stock from cross-site transfer, including the bearing example where a real cross-site match is not operationally useful.

The mechanism is strong but not complete: it concludes that the sample is "not blocked on matching" without testing whether semantic retrieval materially improves identification of the 11 requests lacking part numbers.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The evidence table labels claims as FACT versus INFERENCE and gives confidence levels, including "High on rows; Med on the inference" for local stock not being a transfer candidate.
It explicitly downgrades availability certainty because "the stock view is four weeks older" and says to verify HA-0022 and ME-0006 rather than treating negative availability as final.

"Actionable now 6" and "only 6 clear them cross-site" are somewhat stronger than the stale-source evidence supports, although the instruction to hold POs pending live confirmation appropriately limits the operational risk.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: The recommendation reframes the decision from headline search savings to candidate value versus operationally actionable value: "Defer the semantic-search pilot; this sample is not blocked on matching."
It provides reversible actions: "Raise the 6 but hold the POs," cancel only after a live screen, verify reservations, and obtain revision and qualification sign-offs.

The recommendation protects against unsafe transfers, but deferring the pilot may be premature because semantic search could still be useful as candidate generation for the 11 blank-identifier requests.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission actively tests and rejects several plausible explanations or actions: matching does not imply transfer, the pilot does not automatically avoid $166k, the bearing transfer is unnecessary, negative global availability may be lag, and description similarity is not identity.
It preserves a viable alternative by noting that "a different-looking seal was interchangeable," so blank-description matches require checks rather than automatic refusal.
It also states what evidence would revive conditional candidates, including live screens, confirmed part numbers, revision interchangeability, and qualification sign-offs.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: It prioritizes "Live local screens for the 7 own-site rows" as the cheapest, highest-leverage next evidence and explains the decision impact on $29,242 of POs.
It separately requests confirmed part numbers for the 11 blanks, live availability for HA-0022 and ME-0006, revision A/B interchangeability, and qualification decisions for SITE_SPECIFIC_CHECK rows.
These requests are specific, decision-linked, and mostly minimal rather than a generic request for more data.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "This sample is not blocked on matching" is too categorical: the 11 requests without part numbers are precisely where semantic candidate generation may reduce manual identification effort, even if it cannot authorize transfer.

"Actionable now 6" and "only 6 clear them cross-site" should be described as conditionally actionable because the global stock snapshot is stale and some availability claims require live confirmation.

The statement that the exact join "resolves all 13 requests carrying one" is plausible but insufficiently demonstrated in the submission at row-and-field level; identity resolution does not itself resolve revision, UOM, qualification, reservation, or temporal consistency.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The semantic-search pilot should proceed in a constrained role as candidate generation, not as an autonomous transfer decision. The exact joins show that manufacturer part numbers are the stronger identity path, but the 11 blank-identifier requests and the seal interchangeability example leave a meaningful retrieval problem. A pilot can be justified if it produces ranked candidates only, applies revision/UOM/qualification/reservation filters, reports candidate value separately from actionable value, and requires engineering and live-availability confirmation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a small blinded candidate-generation test on the 11 blank-identifier requests using normalized descriptions plus manufacturer-part-number boosts, then measure precision at the top-k against engineering-confirmed equivalence and the number/value of candidates that survive revision, UOM, qualification, reservation, and freshness checks. This would directly test whether matching is truly not the bottleneck before deferring the pilot.
